14226-lobo-rag-and-vixen-being-the-perso:
Ernest Seton-Thompson gathered true animal histories in Lobo, Rag, and Vixen, selected from Wild Animals I Have Known and published by Scribner's in 1908. A note insists the stories are true, and that animal sounds, signs, touches, tastes, and smells form a language he merely translates into English. Illustrations show Lobo and Blanca, Redruff saving Runtie, and Rag's tussles.

Three lives anchor the book. Lobo, the great wolf, rules his range until hunters close in. Redruff, a young partridge, learns the November moon madness, when first-year birds fly wildly into wires, lighthouses, and city streets. Rag, a cottontail, escapes dogs, foxes, cats, skunks, hawks, and men daily, once playing hound against skunk and once fleeing a hunter's ferret. Natural history, told as biography, taught young readers to see animals as persons with habits, fears, and wits.
doe-osti-2583524-blending-pipeline-analy:
User manual NREL/TP-5400-87790, by Jamie Kee, Evan Reznicek, Mark Chung, and Kevin Topolski, documents BlendPATH, NREL's tool for asking what hydrogen does to a natural gas pipeline network. Blend in hydrogen and everything shifts: pressures, flows, compressor duty, and the heating value delivered to customers. BlendPATH simulates the network as a system of nonlinear equations and solves it at steady state.

The manual walks users through the hydraulic model, pipe physics, compressor stations, and constraint handling, plus how the model was verified. An assessment layer segments a transmission network and checks design pressures segment by segment. Where a blend breaks the rules, three fixes are costed: replacing pipe directly, adding parallel loops, or installing more compression. A cost model prices new pipe and each remedy. For utilities weighing hydrogen blending, the manual turns a policy question into an engineering calculation with a price tag.
doe-osti-2588038-modeling-volumetric-ene: When heavy fluid sits on light fluid it ripples, and this DOE report models that wobble. The pages detail the driven simulations. The physicists get their data. The ripple was Rayleigh-Taylor. The simulations were driven. The wobble was fluid.
doe-osti-3015243-commercialization-of-pu:
Commercializing pumped storage hydropower is assessed in ANL-25/5, an Argonne-led HydroWIRES report dated December 2025, written with four other national laboratories for the Water Power Technologies Office. Pumped storage supplies most long-duration storage on the United States grid today, with a median duration near 12 hours, yet new projects are slow to build.

Of 96 proposed new projects counted, 78 are closed-loop designs whose reservoirs sit apart from natural water bodies. Closed-loop plants allow freer siting and generally lower environmental impact, and since 2019 qualifying projects can use a two-year Federal Energy Regulatory Commission licensing track when impacts are documented as low. The study then works through the cost, market, and permitting barriers that still stall the pipeline.
doe-osti-3385037-fielding-interface-for-:
Sandia National Laboratories report SAND2026-23547, printed July 2026, documents the fielding interface for the AEDR, by Michael E. Partridge. The report is an engineering build record: a requirements chapter with deliverables and interface definitions opens it, and backward compatibility with the earlier 3AMP system gets its own section.

The design's core is a serializer and deserializer, SerDes, that converts data between forms for transmission. Chapters detail the SerDes interface implementation and its algorithm for 8b/10b encoding, then an FPGA performing the symbol conversion. A high-speed USB peripheral controller follows, with the QuickUSB chip's configuration settings for this device spelled out, and a final how-to chapter covers programming the Altera Max 10 FPGA. Anyone rebuilding or maintaining the unit has the full chain in one volume.
doe-osti-3599478-on-the-recombination-of:
Brookhaven technical note BNL-230134-2026-TECH, numbered CA/AP/758 and dated August 2026, studies how high-energy hadrons recombine with electrons. Seven authors are printed: Gang Wang, Dmitry Kayran, Nikhil Bachhawat, Yichao Jing, Vladimir N. Litvinenko, Jun Ma, and Igor Pinayev. They work at Brookhaven and Stony Brook University. The setting is a beam line where ions and electrons travel together, as in an electron cooler.

When the two beams share the same speed, the recombination rate peaks. Scanning electron energy while watching that rate is thus a way to match the beam energies. The team derived formulas for how the rate falls off as the energies part. Their math takes the sideways motion of both particle types into account. They then applied the formulas to data from the Coherent electron Cooler tests at RHIC. In those runs, the measured rate fell more slowly than energy spread alone would predict.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-KarneiRobertFDr:
Two House Select Committee on Assassinations staffers, Jim Kelly and Andy Purdy, wrote a memorandum on August 29, 1977. It reports their August 23 interview with Dr. Robert F. Karnei Jr. Karnei had taken part in President Kennedy's autopsy, which made him a witness the committee needed.

The autopsy remained the case's most contested ground, and the committee worked it doctor by doctor. A staff memo fixed what one participant said in 1977 about a night in 1963. Such memos became the committee's memory, and this one preserves Karnei's turn in that record. He spoke as a participant in the autopsy, not as a later commentator on it.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-SpockBenjaminDr: Dr Benjamin Spock - the baby doctor turned activist - is the title subject of this declassified US government document. The Internet Archive lists no date, no agency, no content note. Text not publicly found. A famous name in an empty file.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-StewartDavidDr_: Writing in a Lebanon, Tennessee newspaper in March 1967, Carl Wallace reported the charges of Dr. David Stewart. Stewart cited coverups and deception in the official account of the Kennedy assassination. His claims joined a growing wave of public doubt about the Warren Commission in the years right after its report. The article preserves a small-town paper giving space to a local critic of the official story.
lobo-rag-and-vixen-being-the-personal-hi:
Ernest Thompson Seton selected these animal histories from his earlier collection. Charles Scribner's Sons published the volume in New York in 1908. The stories first appeared in Wild Animals I Have Known. Seton insists these are true histories of the animals described.

Animals lack full language, he explains, but communicate richly. Sounds, signs, touches, tastes, and smells answer language's purpose. Seton merely translates that system into English for readers. Lobo and Blanca, Redruff, and Raggylug fill the illustrated tales. Lobo and Blanca face page eighteen in the illustrations. Redruff saving Runtie illustrates the grouse story at page sixty.
nasa-tm-19680024730-an-analysis-of-an-el:
Roger B. Stewart of Langley Research Center analyzes an electromagnetically driven confined vortex in this paper, presented in September 1967. The vortex spins inside a chamber with concentric cylindrical electrodes. Gas flows radially through the chamber while electromagnetic forces drive the swirling motion.

Stewart studies flow with high positive radial Reynolds numbers, meaning strong outward flow. Earlier closed-form solutions by Kessey and Lewellen covered inward flow cases. Stewart adapts those solutions for velocity, pressure, and induced magnetic field with outward flow. An approximate energy equation adds the temperature picture. The work offers insight into high energy gas flows inside such devices. Those flows matter for electric propulsion and plasmadynamics research.
